title.en: Show that nuclear density is independent of A

say.en: If an atom were the size of the Chinnaswamy stadium, its nucleus would be smaller than a marble at the centre, yet it holds almost all the mass. In this lesson: Use R equals R 0A^(1 over 3).
Show that nuclear density is independent of A.

body.en: Scattering experiments with fast electrons and alpha particles show that the *radius* of a nucleus of mass number $A$ is $R = R_0A^{1/3}$, with $R_0 \approx 1.2$ fm ($1$ fm $= 10^{-15}$ m). So the volume of a nucleus is proportional to $A$.
body.kn: A ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯ ನ್ಯೂಕ್ಲಿಯಸ್‌ನ ತ್ರಿಜ್ಯ R = R₀A^(1/3), R₀ ≈ 1.2 fm. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಘನಫಲ A ಗೆ ಅನುಪಾತೀಯ.

title.en: Board: how big is a nucleus?

narration.en: Let us see how nuclear size grows with mass number and why all nuclei have the same density.

say.en: The radius grows as the cube root of A, with R₀ about 1.2 femtometre.
Aluminium-27: cube root of 27 is 3, so R = 3.6 fm. Eight times the nucleons gives only twice the radius.
Mass is A times m and volume is four-thirds π R₀³ A, so A cancels in the density.

text.en: A cancels: same for all nuclei

say.en: The density is about 2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg per cubic metre, some 10¹⁴ times that of water.

say.en: Scattering experiments show R equals R0 A^(1 over 3) with R0 is approximately 1.2 fm. So the volume grows in step with A: every nucleus has about the same density, about 2.3 times 10 to the power 17 kilograms per cubic metre, whatever its size. The circle is drawn to scale in femtometres.

body.en: The mass of a nucleus is about $A$ u and its volume is $\tfrac43\pi R_0^3A$, so the *density* does not depend on $A$. It is about $2.3\times10^{17}$ kg/m³, roughly $10^{14}$ times the density of water. Neutron stars are made of matter this dense.
body.kn: ನ್ಯೂಕ್ಲಿಯಸ್‌ನ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ ಮತ್ತು ಘನಫಲ ಎರಡೂ A ಗೆ ಅನುಪಾತೀಯ; ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಸಾಂದ್ರತೆ ಸ್ಥಿರ, ಸುಮಾರು 2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg/m³.

problem.en: Find the radius of the ²⁷Al nucleus and its density. (R₀ = 1.2 fm, 1 u = 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ kg)

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Find the radius of the ²⁷Al nucleus and its density. (R₀ = 1.2 fm, 1 u = 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ kg)

say.en: Let us solve this together. Find the radius of the to the power 27Al nucleus and its density. (R 0 equals 1.2 fm, 1 u equals 1.66 times 10 to the power minus 27 kilograms).
R equals 1.2 times 27^(1 over 3) equals 1.2 times 3 equals 3.6 fm.
Mass is approximately 27 times 1.66 times 10 to the power minus 27 kilograms is approximately 4.48 times 10 to the power minus 26 kilograms.
rho equals m over (4 over 3 pi R cubed) equals 4.48 times 10 to the power minus 26 over (1.95 times 10 to the power minus 43) is approximately 2.3 times 10 to the power 17 kilograms per cubic metre.
So the answer is R equals 3.6 fm, rho is approximately 2.3 times 10 to the power 17 kilograms per cubic metre.
